card.name: Plural nouns and verbs after list openers
card.fires_on: Content words right after a setup phrase such as "There are", "some", "told residents to" or "e.g.,", where a plural noun or base-form verb comes next. It fires in general web prose more than in drug-label text.

modes.label: Noun after "There are/were"
modes.description: A plural noun or adjective that opens a list or description following "There are", "There were" or "are".
modes.example: There are<< customs>> and rituals and beliefs that our ancestors were

modes.label: Verb after "to" or "e.g.,"
modes.description: A base-form verb that starts an instruction or action after "to" or "e.g.,".
modes.example: Officials have placed the volcano on yellow alert (alert level Yellow II) and have told residents to<< prepare>> in case evacuation becomes necessary.

modes.label: Noun as subject after "some"
modes.description: A noun after a quantity word in a news report.
modes.example: According to reports from Reuters some<< buildings>> in the Venezuelan countryside were damaged, but
